rationale: Settle the snapshot question's peer variant by source, since the forwarded form repeats the same derivation on every receiving node: each peer's snapshot call compares the requested index against that peer's own decided index - also drifted to 9 in the observed run - and builds from that peer's own range, so the peers end in the same loss rather than a different state, with the caveat that their own snapshots were not sampled. The account is rewritten as a complete current account keeping the witnessed leader-side loss, the corrected counter-argument about the equal case, the follower-side and entry-type variants, and the limits; the question's discriminator now names only what an execution could still add (the peers' own snapshots and the follower-side call).

investigations.discriminator: Whether the peers that receive a forwarded snapshot request, and a follower called directly, show the same empty snapshot in their own reads; the derivation says they compute the same bound and range on their own decided index, so a decisive observation would be their snapshots and their reads after the call sampled directly.

interpretations.rationale: Witnessed, with the discriminator's variants now settled by source. Witness: with the drift in place (accepted 9, 9 and 6, decided 9, six indices of content), snapshot(Some(8), false) returned Ok on the leader, its compacted index became 8, and the snapshot reachable at index 0 held zero entry ids where the log had five decided entries (e70b8baa087246c78ea3a64f24b8e97c events 0-5); the comparisons requiring the compacted index to reach six and the snapshot to hold five entries were violated at the call event. Variants: (i) a request equal to the drifted decided index is not protected, because the equal case maps it to the decided log without the StopSign (8) which still exceeds the content (6) - this corrects my earlier counter-argument; (ii) the bound is computed on whichever node receives the call, so a follower with the same drifted decided index accepts the same request, and the local_only flag only decides whether the request is forwarded; (iii) the forwarded form repeats the derivation on every peer - each peer's own snapshot call compares the requested index against its own decided index (which in the observed run was also 9) and builds from its own range, so the peers end in the same loss rather than a different state, while the sampling here covered only their accepted and decided indexes (events 4, 5); (iv) the form the loss takes is whatever the entry type's Snapshot::create gives to an empty slice, which for this entry type is an empty snapshot that the reads then report for the compacted region.

knowledge.assertion: the snapshot bound comes from the decided index alone
the snapshot path accepted a drifted bound and produced a snapshot holding none of the entries
the recorded accepted and decided indexes drift one index per re-synchronization round

counterevidence: The call itself returned Ok, so nothing in its result signals the loss; the witness is the compacted index together with the number of entries the produced snapshot holds.
The user supplied the index 8; the documented note allows any index up to the decided index, which was 9, so the request was inside the documented allowance rather than a caller error.
The apparent protection offered by the equal case does not hold in the observed state: it lowers the bound from 9 to 8, which is still above the content (6).
limitations: The consequence depends on the entry type's snapshot: here the snapshot records its input entries and is empty for an empty slice; an entry type that reconstructs state differently could behave differently.

The peers' own snapshots were not sampled in this run; the claim that they end in the same loss is read from the derivation that each peer computes its own bound and range, not from their observed snapshots.
The follower-side, equal-index and peer-side variants are argued from the derivation rather than executed; only the leader's call was sampled.

One three-node configuration, three reconnection rounds, one index and one entry type were exercised, and the comparisons tying the before and after samples to their admissions are unknown because of a shared event name in the same execution, so those states are asserted from the sampled operands (events 0-5).
